evidence.note: Runs run_eval.py, notes all six task types pass structural checks, and explicitly pivots to 'validating the underlying logic to guarantee numerical correctness' — cleanly distinguishing structural-valid from correct, above the level-3 conflation.
Decides to 'focus on retrieval_01 since that test passes' — monitors progress by representative task per type rather than tracking all 37 individually; no inventory of the full horizon.
Makes shared-code edits (STS gold min/max condition) but shows no re-verification of downstream/other tasks' numbers afterward — misses the shared-code ripple-detection of higher anchors.
Rationalizes 'offline verification means I don't need to test everything myself,' shifting trust to the harness/verifier instead of maintaining a numerical ledger across tasks.
Ends by checking results.json format and declaring 'Done' — completion resting on structural-green plus trust in the offline verifier, not a completed cross-validation of all 37 tasks.

reasoning: The agent clearly separates 'structurally passing' from 'numerically correct' (steps 51, 84) and notices that numerical validation remains to be done, which lifts it above the level-3 conflation anchor. But it never maintains a clear inventory of the 37 tasks and their per-task status, works only by representative task-per-type, does not re-verify downstream tasks after shared-code edits, and ultimately leans on the offline verifier and structural-green to declare done — falling short of the clear-inventory expectation at level 5. This places it at a 4.
